title: Field stock engine is ~300x slower than the column engine on a large box (blocks M7.3 retirement)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Found in the review of PR #625 (#588, the `camcraft-sim` CLI onto the field engine), 2026-11-09. **This blocks #589**, the column engine's retirement.

**The measurement** (release build, same program and box):

| Engine | `drill_plate.cl`, box -60..60 × -60..60 × -25..0, default cell 0.375 mm (320 × 320) |
|---|---|
| column (old CLI) | ~0.23 s |
| field (#625) | **~79 s** |

That is about **300× slower**. The output is byte-identical, so it's speed only. #26's heavy agreement lane (`stock_field_cost`) reports 0.25-12 ms/move on the golden programs at its own 0.5 mm lattice. A drill program on a large box at the CLI's auto cell is much worse, probably from the field's per-cell march over a 320² lattice for every plunge, or its build cost.

**Why it matters:** #586, #587 and #589 move the app's carried, rest and prior stock and the motion generators onto the field. If those paths see similar ratios, retiring the column engine would make generation and post-time verification far slower. That's a usability regression the agreement suite can't catch, because it measures verdicts, not time.

**Expected:**
1. **Profile** the field engine on this case and name where the time goes: build, per-move cut, or the final `columns()` read-out.
2. **Fix or bound it:** a field-arm auto cell coarser than the column's where the verdict allows, batched cuts, or a faster read-out. Then state a **wall-time budget** in a heavy-lane test, e.g. "a golden program on a 120 mm box completes within N× the column engine", so the regression can't come back silently.
3. **Until then,** #586, #587 and #589 should not land on the field for interactive paths, and #625's CLI notes the cost in `--help`.

**Done means:** the drill_plate case and the golden programs run within a stated budget relative to the column engine, pinned by a heavy-lane timing test.

Related: #26, #584 (the per-brick law exists and holds, but it bounds work per brick, not total wall time), #585, #588 / PR #625, #589.
